title: Population red blood cell folate concentrations for prevention of neural tube defects: Bayesian model
authors: Crider KS, Devine O, Hao L, Dowling NF, Li S, Molloy AM, et al.
population: Data from the China community intervention project with 400 µg/day folic acid (247,831 women, 1993-1995) and a randomised dosing trial in Chinese women of reproductive age (1194 women, 2003-2005)
funder: Funding for salaries of CDC employees was provided by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. No specific funding was provided for this project.
authorConflicts: No financial relationships with organisations that might have an interest in the work.
result: Modelled neural tube defect risk fell as estimated red cell folate at neural tube closure (day 28 of gestation) rose: 25.4 (95% uncertainty interval 20.8 to 31.2) per 10,000 births at 500 nmol/L, and about 6 per 10,000 at 1180 (1050 to 1340) nmol/L, with risk substantially attenuated above about 1000 nmol/L. The authors propose about 1000 nmol/L as an optimal population red cell folate threshold. Model parameters are in the appendix; no additional data available.
